name: ADMX
summary: ADMX is a major QCD axion dark-matter search using cryogenic microwave cavities, with successive phases at LLNL and the University of Washington.
detection_principle: A static field converts axions to microwave photons; cavity tuning scans axion masses while low-noise receivers measure narrowband power.

status.label: Listed as an ongoing experiment on the university's 2025 project page
status.evidence: The University of Washington's 2025 project description explicitly discusses ADMX operation, new channels and upgrades.

timeline.event: Extended Search for the Invisible Axion with the Axion Dark Matter Experiment

collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Study type
key_parameters.value: Low-mass microwave-cavity axion searches; scan intervals differ between publications

key_parameters.name: Scan published in 2025
key_parameters.value: 1.10–1.31 GHz, approximately 4.54–5.41 μeV; see the run's paper for model-specific sensitivity.

phases.name: Sidecar
phases.description: High-frequency auxiliary-cavity R&D within the same project; not counted as a separate experiment in this catalog.

results.summary: The 2019 extended search reached benchmark invisible-axion sensitivity in its scanned interval, without reporting an axion discovery.
The published 1.10–1.31 GHz search reaches extended-KSVZ sensitivity, without claiming axion discovery.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
